key_insight: RadSight argues that reliable medical multimodal AI depends first on strong low-level visual perception, not just better clinical language generation.
clinical_relevance: For radiology workflows, improving lesion-level perception and spatial grounding could make model outputs more trustworthy for diagnosis and report support.
method: Built Perception-Bench, a 1.13M-sample benchmark covering 2D and 3D radiology across six tasks.
Designed RadSight with a dual 2D/3D encoder to preserve native image spatial structure.
Trained the model with a four-stage curriculum from visual-language alignment to diagnosis and interpretation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that RadSight outperformed existing medical MLLMs across all six Perception-Bench dimensions and also improved on public 2D/3D benchmarks.
watch_item: Performance gains in benchmark settings may not fully translate to real-world clinical deployment without external validation across institutions, scanners, and patient populations.
paper_title: RadSight: Towards Perceptually Reliable Multimodal Radiology Image Understanding
